quotes.text: Deep fakes and other AI-generated content is making it difficult to discern facts, discern truth — that’s going to be more present in our lives. And so we need to create a policy that adequately moves in the direction of avoiding problems that lie ahead.

In my view, Congress must play an active role in ensuring that we sufficiently address challenges & explore opportunities of artificial intelligence.

We need to name the problem. Problem identification is how you get to a solution. Having the right people at the table and setting broad goals around inclusion are crucial to harnessing AI’s potential in areas like public health and education.

The best thing we can do is isolate the noise, focus on objectivity, and ensure clear alignment on truth and facts. With responsible AI development, we can build a future where technology enhances democracy rather than undermines it.

In our @Sciencedems hearing today, I discussed how investing in domestic research is key to beating China in the AI innovation race. 

Unfortunately, the Trump administration seems to be rowing in the wrong direction. 

By canceling STEM research grants to fund AI training and deporting international students, Trump is threatening our country’s ability to compete.

Future thinking companies like this are becoming integral to our #BlueEconomy.

Trump's siding with the demands of big tech and billionaires that will profit over the people who could get hurt.

His AI executive order will stop actions to keep Americans safe.

Right now, our laws do not explicitly cover the remote access of technologies via network connections, including the internet or cloud computing services. H.R. 2683 would close this gap by giving the Bureau of Industry and Security statutory authority to control the remote access of items by bad actors who aim to jeopardize our national security or foreign policy interests.
